title: Latent Space Paper Club: AIEWF Special Edition (Test of Time, DeepSeek R1/V3) — VIbhu Sapra
talk_summary: This is a paper-club recap of DeepSeek V3/R1 and the May-28 R1 refresh, focused on model-training science (pure RL, GRPO, distillation, test-time compute scaling) rather than agent-engineering practice.

takeaways.technique: Distill reasoning traces into small cheap models
takeaways.what_they_do: They take long chain-of-thought traces from a strong reasoning model and SFT-distill them into small models (Qwen 8B/32B, Llama 8B/70B), rather than doing native RL on the small model.
takeaways.numbers: 8B distill matches Qwen 235B thinking model; ~10% gain from re-distilling off the better reasoner

takeaways.what_they_do: They only RL on tasks with checkable outcomes (math answer correct, code compiles), which is what made reasoning training work at all.
takeaways.evidence_quote: for code does your code compile if it compiles that's good we can do RL on that

takeaways.what_they_do: Generate many completions, rank with a reward model, discard the bad ones, and fine-tune only on the kept set (600k reasoning + 200k chat samples).
takeaways.evidence_quote: We do rejection sampling on samples that we don't like. We had 800,000 samples that were generated
takeaways.numbers: 800k samples generated, 600k reasoning / 200k general chat kept

takeaways.technique: Test-time compute scaling is a dial, not free
takeaways.what_they_do: The R1 refresh doubled average reasoning tokens (12k→25k) and got large benchmark gains, showing reasoning length is a tunable cost/quality knob.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it reasons more on on average it reasons for 25,000 tokens. So they got the model to do double the reasoning
